text:
alex: Heads-up — escalated from @customer-ops: ACME (SR-4721) seeing streaming responses stop after a reconnect. Client receives a partial JSON object, then an empty final chunk, then the stream reconnects and client replays last buffer which leads to duplicate billing. Logs attached below. :rotating_light:

alex: logs snippet:
```
  recv SSE event: data: {\"id\":\"msg-123\", \"text\":\"...partial...\"}
  connection closed by server (code 1006)
  client reconnect attempt 1 -> auth refresh 200 OK
  recv SSE empty event: data:
  client iter yields EOF (empty string)
  client resends last chunk to server API -> billed tokens: 512 (unexpected)
```

maria: Thanks. Have a repro on a TS app using the browser SDK + AbortController. It looks like when the AbortController triggers during a TransformStream pipeline, the iterator sometimes yields an empty string as the final value instead of completing. Quick repro below. :eyes:

maria: repro (TS):
```ts
const source = new EventSource(url);
const reader = eventSourceToAsyncIterator(source);
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 1200);
for await (const chunk of reader) {
  if (chunk === '') { console.warn('empty final chunk'); }
  // handle chunk
}
```

maria: When the empty final chunk arrives some clients naively append it and then re-request missing tokens; that leads to duplicate billing spikes.

devon: I can repro in Python as well. Using httpx + our py-sdk async iterator, I get the same pattern when canceling the request mid-kv-flush. The iterator yields b'' then raises StopAsyncIteration, but some wrappers treat b'' as produced data.

devon: repro (py):
```py
async with AsyncClient(timeout=10) as client:
    async for chunk in client.stream(\"GET\", sse_url):
        if chunk == b'':
            logger.info("empty final frame")
            continue
        handle(chunk)
```

ryan: Summary of likely root cause: race between stream-close handling and heartbeat/kv-cache flush. If the server closes socket while kernels are flushing, we send a 0-length event then close. Some SDK iterators translate that 0-length event into a final empty data item instead of simply signalling stream end. That can cause client code to treat it as content and retry (or resend), causing duplicates and billing anomalies.

ryan: Immediate mitigations:
- Client-side: treat empty-string or zero-length bytes from iterator as end-of-stream (do not resend). Add dedupe by server-provided msg id if available.
- Server-side: change close ordering to avoid emitting empty data events, and include sequence numbers on each event so clients can dedupe.

maria: I've filed a quickfix PR for the TS SDK to normalize the iterator behavior (ignore empty final chunk). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/812 (WIP). Also adding a test that simulates AbortController close during TransformStream.

devon: For Python I'll add a patch to treat b'' as stream termination in the async iterator wrapper and avoid yielding it. I'll open PR + link in thread.

alex: Can eng-runtime take the server-side change? If we include sequence numbers, customers get a stronger safeguard. @ryan can you own a runtime ticket?

ryan: Yep, creating RT-1198. Plan: adjust SSE flush to guarantee either a final non-empty event with seq N or immediate close with no zero-length event. Also adding seq header: `x-rw-seq: <n>`.

support-bot: Assigned SR-4721 -> ENG-RT-1198. Follow-up scheduled: 2024-12-02 15:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:

alex: Customer notified about workaround (client-side dedupe + SDK patch). Will circle back after PRs land. Thanks all.

support-bot: Note: escalation label set to "billing-impact" and P1 if duplicates observed > 5% of requests.
